question: The most common Harappan seals were _________ in shape.
solution:
The correct answer is __**square**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The majority of Harappan seals were **square in shape**.
 
• These seals typically measured around **2x2 centimeters**.
 
• The seals were often made from **steatite, a soft stone**, which allowed for intricate carvings.
 
• Harappan seals commonly featured **animal motifs and inscriptions in the Harappan script**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Harappan Civilization**

 
 
• The Harappan civilization, also known as the Indus Valley Civilization, was one of the world's earliest urban civilizations, flourishing around 2500 BCE in what is now Pakistan and northwest India.
 
• It is renowned for its advanced urban planning, architecture, and social organization.
 
• The civilization had a writing system, though the Harappan script remains undeciphered.
 
• They engaged in trade with distant regions, including Mesopotamia.
 
 
 
• **Steatite Seals**
 
 
• Steatite, also known as soapstone, is a type of metamorphic rock that is soft and can be easily carved.
 
• Harappan artisans used steatite to create seals, which were then often fired to harden them.
 
• The seals were used for trade and administrative purposes, possibly to stamp goods or documents.
 
 
 
• **Animal Motifs**
 
 
• Common animals depicted on Harappan seals include unicorns, bulls, elephants, and rhinoceroses.
 
• These animal motifs could have had symbolic or religious significance.
 
• The meticulous depiction of these animals suggests a high degree of artistic skill.
 
 
 
• **Harappan Script**
 
 
• The Harappan script is composed of signs and symbols, and it has been found on seals, pottery, and other artifacts.
 
• Despite numerous attempts, the script has not been deciphered, and its language remains unknown.
 
• The script is thought to have been used for administrative and possibly ritualistic purposes.
